$schema_note: Ascend NPU hardware specs for capacity planning and compute simulation. Every numeric field MUST cite a source. Fields marked "unverified" were not confirmed on this machine and MUST NOT be used for acceptance numbers.

sources.npu-smi: Read directly from `npu-smi info` on Ascend hardware (authoritative for this machine).
sources.cann-doc: CANN official documentation / aclnn & AscendC docs shipped under /usr/local/Ascend.
sources.vendor-spec: Vendor datasheet. Cite the exact table; do not round.
sources.measured: Measured on this machine by a recorded run. Attach the trace/log path.

910b3.hbm_capacity_unit: vendor GB (65536 MB as reported by npu-smi); measure usable GiB before quoting capacity
910b3.shape: PCIe add-in card, 1 die per card, 1 device per card
notes: This machine reports 8 cards / 8 devices / 8 dies.
Chip frequency observed at idle was 800 MHz while nominal is 1800 MHz; do not use the idle reading as a compute bound.
Do NOT conflate with 910B2/B4 — the aicore count and HBM differ.

910c.shape: 2 dies per card. Device numbering runs /dev/davinci0..15 on an 8-card server.
notes: CRITICAL: TP/EP degrees count DEVICES, not physical cards. 8 cards = 16 devices.
This machine has no 910C; every 910C number must be sourced from vendor docs or a run on real A3.
unverified: hbm_gb must be filled from the A3 datasheet before any capacity claim.
unverified on this machine. 96GB per die appears in vllm-ascend model tutorials; confirm before use.

hardware_terms.card: A physical PCIe board. A 910B3 card carries 1 die; a 910C card carries 2.
hardware_terms.device: A single compute die addressable as /dev/davinciN. This is what TP/EP/DP degrees count.
hardware_terms.rank: The process-level index mapped onto a device for a given parallel group.
hardware_terms.rule: Every benchmark row MUST state whether its parallelism is in cards or devices. Mixing them silently is the single most common cause of wrong capacity math on Ascend.

memory_scope.hbm: On-die HBM. Reported by npu-smi as HBM-Usage(MB).
memory_scope.host: Host DRAM reachable over PCIe/HCCS. Engram-class embeddings and KV offload may live here.
memory_scope.baseline_resident_note: ~3.2-3.4 GB per card is resident before any user process (driver + exporters). Subtract this before reasoning about a model's headroom.

network.interconnect: HCCL over HCCS / RoCE depending on the server SKU
network.note: Cross-framework benchmarks on Ascend MUST record the HCCL backend and topology; a collective-heavy model's numbers are not comparable across backends.

software_stack_reference.note: npu-smi reports 'Software Version 25.5.2'. CANN toolkit component versions are read from version.cfg. Record BOTH in any benchmark evidence.
